observations: Photo 0 shows a large vehicle drivetrain assembly on the ground with multiple housings, wiring/hoses, and a transfer-case style section; it looks like a combined transmission/transfer case unit rather than a single gearbox alone.
Photo 1 shows another angle of the same/related drivetrain assembly with many attached components and wiring; no clear readable ID plate is visible.
Photo 2 shows the lower/side view of the same assembly; again no clearly readable model/part number tag is visible.

identity.kind: Jeep Wrangler 3.6L 4x4 transmission/gearbox with transfer case (drivetrain assembly)

claims.evidence: Photos show a drivetrain assembly but no readable VIN/part number/ID plate confirming Wrangler 3.6L or the listed years.
No documentation (import/auction sheet) or readable markings in photos to confirm origin or mileage.

risks.risk: Wrong fitment (year/engine/4x4 variant) — the assembly may not match Wrangler 3.6L 2011–2017 or may be a different drivetrain configuration.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the transmission/transfer-case ID tag/part number (and any casting numbers) plus a photo showing the mating bellhousing/transfer-case side.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not confirmed compatible (treated as high risk for fitment).

risks.risk: Not actually a complete gearbox/transfer-case unit as claimed (could be missing parts, sensors, or the wrong sub-assembly).
risks.proof: Photo showing all ports/connectors and the full assembly end-to-end, including what’s included/excluded (starter mount area, sensor plugs, output flanges).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: incomplete/unknown completeness (treated as not guaranteed ready to install).

risks.risk: Condition unknown (may be damaged internally or have leaks) because there’s no test run or fluid condition shown.
risks.proof: Video of a bench test or at minimum photos of fluid condition (drain/fill ports) and any evidence of damage; also a short clip showing it shifting through gears.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: not proven working (treated as not working/unknown).

risks.risk: Transfer case ratio/4x4 system mismatch (e.g., different transfer case type) affecting driveline behavior.
risks.proof: Close-up of transfer case label/part number and any markings indicating the transfer case model/ratio.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst-case: transfer case type not confirmed (treated as incompatible risk).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the transmission/transfer-case ID plate or part number (and casting numbers) from photo angles that make text readable.
Photo of the full assembly showing all included components and any missing sensors/hoses/bolts/connectors.
Video/clip showing it shifts/operates (or a bench test) and confirmation of no major leaks.
Any paperwork from the source (auction/import sheet) showing mileage/condition and vehicle details.
response.reason: The photos show a drivetrain/transmission-like assembly, but there’s no readable ID to confirm the exact Wrangler 3.6L 4x4 years/fitment, and there’s no proof it works. Without those, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
